reasons: Classification is correct: the cap basis (greater of $100,000 or 12 months' charges) and mutuality (Sections 9.1/9.2 mirror each other) already satisfy the fallback, but the fallback also requires carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. Only indemnification payments and bodily injury/tangible property sit outside the cap, so a material fallback term fails — this is a genuine deviation, not an upgrade of an acceptable fallback.

The Section 6 prevailing-provisions language (p0080) affirmatively pulls confidentiality breaches concerning information in the hosting environment inside the Section 9 cap, which supports the materiality of the shortfall rather than being a stylistic gap.

Redline is minimal and actionable and follows the redline guidance: it leaves Sections 9.1/9.2 intact and adds a single mutual 'Excluded Claims' provision (9.3) covering confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, and IP infringement, expressly overriding Section 6's precedence rule so the carve-out actually bites.

Directionally correct for the customer and mutual, so it does not create a one-sided advantage that would invite rejection; it does not disturb the already-favourable Section 10 exclusion that carves out Customer's payment obligations.

The failed deterministic check ('cap references 12 months of fees or a fixed floor') is a false negative: the inserted text is a carve-out sentence, not a restatement of the cap, and the existing cap language already meets the 12-month/fixed-floor basis. Insertion point p0121 is the tail of Section 9.2, an appropriate location even though that paragraph was not in the cited original set.

Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position, acknowledges the acceptable cap, and offers the narrower fallback carve-out set; no double-flagging (the records/data exclusion in 9.1(2) is expressly deferred to the data rules).
